UH Graduate School How to Apply

applicationPortal.value: Applicants complete the University of Houston Graduate School application through ApplyWeb and also complete the Moores School of Music supplemental application through the Moores application portal. Moores states that graduate applicants must meet University of Houston Graduate School requirements, apply separately to the Moores School, and pass an audition on the principal instrument or voice. Graduate applicants submit three letters of recommendation, official transcripts to UH Graduate Admissions, the Moores supplemental application, and any required high-quality video recording or supplemental materials in the Moores portal. Graduate assistantship application is optional through the Moores School of Music application.

applicationFee.value: UH Graduate School application fee: $50 for domestic applicants, $80 for international applicants, and $25 for non-degree certificate-based programs. Limited application fee waivers are available, and applicants should check with the program regarding eligibility. Moores School of Music also requires a separate supplemental application through its portal; the public Moores page does not list a separate supplemental fee amount.

auditionRequirements.value: Moores School of Music applicants must pass an audition on the principal instrument or voice. The Moores graduate admissions page requires a high-quality video recording for all performance, collaborative piano, music education, and conducting applicants, with specific video and audition requirements in the Moores application portal. The current Moores Graduate Audition & Application Requirements PDF, Rev. 250919, lists piano prescreening and audition requirements. Prescreening applicants upload at least 10 minutes of music that best represents their playing, with selections from any part of the audition repertoire. Applicants are notified if they pass the prescreening round and are invited to a live audition. Both live and video-recorded auditions are used as the audition for scholarships. The MM Piano audition may include an examination of sight-reading skills.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: Applicants should upload at least 10 minutes of music that best represents their playing. Prescreening repertoire: Selections can be from any part of the audition repertoire. Prescreening repertoire: Applicants will be notified if they pass the prescreening round and are invited to a live audition. Final audition repertoire: Master of Music in Piano Performance or Piano Performance & Pedagogy applicants prepare three fully memorized selections from the standard classical piano repertoire. Final audition repertoire: The selections must represent contrasting musical periods and styles. Final audition repertoire: The audition should be approximately 20 minutes in length. Final audition repertoire: Some examination of sight-reading skills may also be part of the audition.

deadlines.value: Moores public admissions page does not publish a static calendar date for the current graduate priority music application deadline. It states that applicants should submit the Moores supplemental application by the priority deadline, recommended, and that specific pre-screening video and audition requirements, details, deadlines, and application requirements are in the Moores application portal. Applicants should use the Moores application portal as the official source for current submission and audition deadlines. Both live and video-recorded auditions are used as the audition for scholarships, so scholarship-sensitive applicants should follow the portal priority deadline rather than waiting for later availability.

englishScores.value: Minimum scores: TOEFL iBT 79 or higher. Minimum scores: TOEFL paper-based 550 or higher. Minimum scores: IELTS 6.5 overall. Minimum scores: Duolingo English Test 105. Minimum scores: PTE overall 53 or higher. Notes: All graduate applicants, regardless of citizenship status, must demonstrate proficiency in English unless exempt. Test scores must be valid and reportable at the time of application submission, within the last two years for TOEFL, IELTS, Pearson, or Duolingo. TOEFL scores must be received directly from ETS, and the University of Houston ETS institutional code is 6870. Completion of Level 6 of UH's Language and Culture Center may satisfy the requirement only where accepted by the graduate program. Departments may require higher minimum TOEFL or IELTS scores.

applicationPortal.value: University of Houston's Moores School Piano page describes Keyboard Collaborative Arts as available at the MM and DMA levels and says the collaborative piano degrees prepare graduates for solo performance, instrumental and vocal collaboration, choral accompanying, vocal coaching, and collegiate accompanist work. Applicants complete the University of Houston Graduate School application through ApplyWeb and also complete the Moores School of Music supplemental application through the Moores application portal. The current Moores audition PDF uses the program label Master of Music in Keyboard Collaborative Arts for this pathway.

auditionRequirements.value: Moores requires a high-quality video recording for all performance, collaborative piano, music education, and conducting applicants, with specific video and audition requirements in the Moores application portal. The Moores Graduate Audition & Application Requirements PDF, Rev. 250919, lists prescreening requirements for Keyboard Collaborative Arts. Prescreening applicants upload at least 10 minutes of music that best represents their playing, with selections from any part of the audition repertoire, and are notified if they pass the prescreening round and are invited to a live audition. If applicants for the Collaborative Arts program are unable to perform with collaborative partners, they should notify Professor Timothy Hester. At the audition, applicants must present a full transcript of the academic career, a musical vita, and a repertoire list. Sight-reading of instrumental repertoire, sight-reading of vocal music with the vocal line incorporated into the accompaniment, and transposition of a song up or down a half or whole step may also be evaluated.

repertoireRequirements.value: Prescreening repertoire: Applicants should upload at least 10 minutes of music that best represents their playing. Prescreening repertoire: Selections can be from any part of the audition repertoire. Prescreening repertoire: Applicants will be notified if they pass the prescreening round and are invited to a live audition. Final audition repertoire: Applicants auditioning for the M.M. in Keyboard Collaborative Arts must prepare three representative works in different styles and varied instrumentation. Final audition repertoire: Examples include a Baroque flute sonata, a Romantic string sonata, and a modern vocal work. Additional repertoire notes: If applicants are unable to perform with collaborative partners, they should notify Professor Timothy Hester. Additional repertoire notes: The following may also be evaluated: sight-reading of instrumental repertoire; sight-reading of vocal music, incorporating the playing of the vocal line into the accompaniment; transposition of a song up or down a half or whole step.
